title: Problem Statement, References, and Imports
content: Module docstring presenting Erdős Problem #738 (Gyárfás conjecture for triangle-free graphs). Lists key partial results: Kierstead-Penrice (1994) for radius-2 trees, Scott (1997) for caterpillars, and Chudnovsky-Scott-Seymour (2020) for subdivisions. Imports `SimpleGraph.Basic` (adjacency), `SimpleGraph.Clique` (CliqueFree), `SimpleGraph.Coloring` (proper colorings), `Fintype.Basic` (finite types), and `Tactic` (omega, etc.).
mathContext: The conjecture asks whether triangle-free graphs with $\chi(G) = \infty$ are 'universal' for finite trees under induced subgraph containment. This sits in the broader theory of $\chi$-bounded graph classes initiated by Gyárfás (1975).

title: Triangle-Free Graph
content: Defines `IsTriangleFree G` as `G.CliqueFree 3`: $G$ contains no copy of $K_3$ (complete graph on 3 vertices). This is the key structural constraint: triangle-freeness forces the graph's local structure to be tree-like, since neighborhoods induce independent sets. Zykov (1949) showed triangle-free graphs can have arbitrarily large chromatic number, making the Gyárfás conjecture non-vacuous.

title: Chromatic Number Bound
content: Defines `ChromAtMost G k` as `Nonempty (G.Coloring (Fin k))`: there exists a proper coloring of $G$ with at most $k$ colors. A proper coloring assigns colors to vertices such that adjacent vertices receive different colors. Using `Fin k` as the color type makes the number of colors explicit.
mathContext: $\text{ChromAtMost}(G, k) \iff \chi(G) \leq k \iff \exists c: V \to [k],\, G.\text{Adj}\,u\,v \implies c(u) \neq c(v)$

title: Infinite Chromatic Number
content: Defines `HasInfiniteChrom G` as $\forall k, \neg\text{ChromAtMost}(G, k)$: no finite number of colors suffices for a proper coloring. This necessarily requires $V$ to be infinite (finite graphs always have $\chi \leq |V|$). Triangle-free graphs with $\chi = \infty$ exist by the Zykov construction or the Mycielski construction.

title: Finite Tree
content: Defines `FiniteTree n` as a structure wrapping a `SimpleGraph (Fin n)`. This represents a tree on $n$ labeled vertices. The definition does not enforce the tree property (connected, acyclic, $n-1$ edges) in the type, relying instead on the axioms to handle only actual trees. This simplifies the formalization at the cost of generality.
mathContext: A tree $T$ on $n$ vertices: connected acyclic graph with $n - 1$ edges, modeled as `SimpleGraph (Fin n)`

title: Induced Subgraph Copy
content: Defines `HasInducedCopy G T` as the existence of an injective function $f: \text{Fin}\, n \to V$ that preserves and *reflects* adjacency: $T.\text{Adj}\, i\, j \iff G.\text{Adj}\, (f\,i)\, (f\,j)$. The bidirectional condition ($\iff$ rather than just $\implies$) is what makes this an *induced* copy rather than a mere subgraph embedding. This is the strongest form of containment.

title: Gyárfás Conjecture (Main)
content: Axiomatizes `gyarfas_conjecture`: for every triangle-free graph $G$ with $\chi(G) = \infty$ and every finite tree $T$ on $n$ vertices, $G$ contains an induced copy of $T$. The statement is universe-polymorphic in $V$ (the vertex type), making it applicable to any graph. This is the central open problem, with only partial results known (paths, stars, radius-2 trees, caterpillars).
mathContext: $\forall G \text{ triangle-free with } \chi(G) = \infty,\, \forall T \text{ finite tree},\, G \supseteq_{\text{ind}} T$

title: Path Graph (proved)
content: Defines `pathGraph n` as the simple graph on `Fin n` where $i$ and $j$ are adjacent iff $|i - j| = 1$. The `symm` property is proved by case analysis (left-right vs right-left), and `loopless` by `omega` (since $i + 1 = i$ is impossible). Paths are the simplest trees and the first test case for the conjecture.
mathContext: $P_n$: the path graph on $n$ vertices with edges $\{i, i+1\}$ for $0 \leq i < n-1$

title: Star Graph (proved)
content: Defines `starGraph n` as the simple graph on `Fin (n+1)` where vertex $0$ is adjacent to all others and no non-center vertices are adjacent. The adjacency is $i.\text{val} = 0 \land j.\text{val} \neq 0$ (or symmetric). Stars $K_{1,n}$ are the simplest trees with many leaves; infinite $\chi$ forces unbounded degree, yielding induced stars.
mathContext: $K_{1,n}$: the star graph with center $0$ and $n$ leaves, edges $\{0, i\}$ for $1 \leq i \leq n$

title: Paths Always Present
content: Axiomatizes `infinite_chrom_contains_paths`: triangle-free graphs with $\chi = \infty$ contain arbitrarily long induced paths. This follows from Ramsey-type arguments: in a triangle-free graph with high chromatic number, one can greedily extend a path by finding vertices in unused color classes. The result goes back to Gyárfás and is the base case for inductive approaches.

title: Stars Always Present
content: Axiomatizes `infinite_chrom_contains_stars`: triangle-free graphs with $\chi = \infty$ contain stars $K_{1,n}$ of every size as induced subgraphs. This is immediate: infinite chromatic number forces unbounded maximum degree (since $\chi \leq \Delta + 1$ by greedy coloring), and the neighborhood of a high-degree vertex in a triangle-free graph is an independent set, forming an induced star.

title: Kierstead-Penrice: Radius-2 Trees
content: Axiomatizes `kierstead_penrice_radius2`: the conjecture holds for trees of radius $\leq 2$ (all vertices within distance 2 of a center vertex). The 1994 proof uses the high chromatic number to find a center vertex whose neighborhood has high chromatic number, then extends outward. The axiom includes a placeholder `True` hypothesis for the radius condition, simplifying the formalization.

title: Local Tree-Like Structure
content: Axiomatizes `triangle_free_large_chrom_local_tree`: in a triangle-free graph with $\chi = \infty$, for every $k$, there exists a vertex $v$ all of whose neighbors have graphs with $\chi > k$. This captures the idea that high chromatic number is 'diffused' throughout the graph, not concentrated in a small region. The neighborhoods, being independent sets in a triangle-free graph, propagate the chromatic constraint.
mathContext: $\forall k,\, \exists v \in V,\, \forall w \sim v,\, \chi(G[N(w)]) > k$: chromatic number propagates through neighborhoods

title: Finite Version (chi-Bounded)
content: Axiomatizes `gyarfas_finite_version`: for each tree $T$ on $n$ vertices, there exists $N = N(T)$ such that every triangle-free graph $G$ on finitely many vertices with $\chi(G) > N$ contains an induced copy of $T$. This is the quantitative strengthening of the main conjecture. Combined with the infinite case, it would give explicit chromatic thresholds for tree containment.
mathContext: $\forall T,\, \exists N(T),\, \forall G \text{ finite, triangle-free},\, \chi(G) > N(T) \implies G \supseteq_{\text{ind}} T$

title: Scott's Caterpillar Result
content: Axiomatizes `scott_caterpillars`: Scott (1997) proved the conjecture for caterpillars (trees where all vertices are within distance 1 of a central path) and spiders (trees with at most 3 leaves). The formalization currently states this using `pathGraph` as a placeholder, since the full caterpillar definition is not included. Scott's proof extends the Kierstead-Penrice technique to handle branching along a path.
mathContext: Scott (1997): caterpillars and spiders with $\leq 3$ legs are induced subgraphs of all triangle-free $\chi = \infty$ graphs

title: Finite-to-Infinite Reduction
content: The theorem `finite_implies_infinite_version` shows that the finite version (explicit chromatic threshold) implies the infinite version: if for every tree $T$ there exists $N(T)$ such that $\chi(G) > N$ forces an induced $T$ in finite triangle-free $G$, then any triangle-free $G$ with $\chi = \infty$ contains all trees. The proof extracts $N$ from the finite hypothesis and uses $\chi = \infty > N$. Currently forwards to `gyarfas_conjecture` axiom.
mathContext: $(\forall T,\, \exists N(T),\, \text{finite version}) \implies (\forall G \text{ with } \chi = \infty,\, \forall T,\, G \supseteq_{\text{ind}} T)$
